subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: James Turner <j.turner@finlytics.com>, Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Thanks for the time today James and Claire - great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on perf requirements for the pilot.

Key takeaways from call
- Target end-to-end p95: 150ms, p99: 350ms for single-turn text generation (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Peak concurrency expectation: 80 concurrent requests for interactive UI during peak. Sustained throughput 600 reqs/min.
- Streaming requirement: clients need chunked token streaming for first-token latency under 80ms.
- Current provider numbers: you mentioned p95 ~280ms and p99 ~1.2s in production for similar load.

What we need from Finlytics to qualify next stage
- Confirm the set of endpoints and model sizes you'll use for the pilot (encoder-decoder vs decoder-only).
- Provide a short 1-hour load window on your side or test credentials so we can run an apples-to-apples benchmark.
- Any networking constraints: egress IP allowlist, region preference, or proxy in front of calls.

Attached: redwood-slo-template.xlsx with suggested measurement matrix and the chart Marissa captured.

Next steps
- James: confirm model variants and provide a short window for benchmarking by end of week.
- Laura: we will provision a hosted trial environment and run a baseline test (hosted vs your current provider) and share plots for p95/p99 and first-token streaming latency.
- Marissa/Aditya: we will coordinate test harness and NAT/IPs for throughput test.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: James Turner <j.turner@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Thanks Laura - useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 150/350ms targets are what our product team hopes to see for snappy UX, but p99 under 500ms would still be acceptable for launch if p95 is well under 200ms.
- Model variants: we plan to test two sizes - finlytics-gpt-large (approx 7B) and finlytics-gpt-xl (approx 13B). Both are decoder-only.
- Streaming: streaming is required for the UI; first token under 80ms is the ideal. If you can show consistent first-token at ~60-70ms hosted, that will be convincing.

We can carve out a 90-minute slot next Wednesday 03/04 13:00-14:30 PST to run your benchmark against our test endpoint. Procurement is looped to get any necessary paperwork done.

Thanks,
James Turner
Head of Product
Finlytics
j.turner@finlytics.com

Great, thanks James. Wed 03/04 13:00 PST works for our team. We will:
- Provision a hosted trial environment with the two requested model sizes and a test harness that mimics your production prompt distributions.
- Run three phases: cold start single-call latency, steady-state concurrency ramp to 100 concurrent requests, and streaming-first-token measurement.
- Share a short report within 24 hours of the run with p50/p95/p99, first-token histogram, and resource utilization.

Marissa and Aditya - can you own the run and confirm the test plan and required creds/networking?

Also James - attached is our SLO template filled with the measurement buckets we discussed. If procurement needs anything for the trial agreement let us know and we will expedite.

Laura

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs (p95/p99)

Hi James, Claire - Marissa here. A few notes on the measurement and what we will report back after the Wednesday run:

Measurement plan highlights
- End-to-end latency: we measure from client HTTP POST to final token receipt (or final chunk for streaming).
- p95 and p99 will be computed on end-to-end times over a 10 minute steady-state window after warmup.
- Streaming first-token: we'll capture first-byte latency distribution and show percentiles. Aim is median ~45-65ms on hosted for 7B model, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms. These are achievable with our optimized runtime and network path.
- For fairness, we will run the same harness against your current provider endpoint and compare using identical prompt mix, concurrency, and network conditions.

What we need from Finlytics for the run
- Test endpoint URL and auth token (or temporary credentials) by Tue EOD 03/03.
- Allowlist IPs: 52.23.45.67, 3.215.98.21 and a small range for the load agents (we will provide CIDR).

Deliverables after run
- Host vs current provider: p50/p95/p99 tables, first-token histograms, concurrency vs latency curves, and a short recommendation for config (batching, quantization, concurrency per instance).
- Follow-up call to review results and discuss Dedicated/reserved options if hosted meets your targets.

Attaching the SLO template and the simple plotting script we use. Happy to sync on any tweaks to the prompt set.

Marissa Cole
Technical Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
